journey.note: Tribunal took functional disability at 25% (half of the 50% in the doctor's certificate) and awarded compensation with 6% interest a year from the date of the petition.
Insurer's appeal partly allowed: disability cut from 25% to 20% and the award reduced.
Injured man's appeal allowed: the High Court cut the disability without a plausible reason, so its judgment was set aside and the tribunal's award with interest restored.

extraction.family_summary: A man riding pillion on a motorcycle broke bones in both forearms in a January 2013 accident and needed surgery with plates and screws. In June 2014 the tribunal awarded Rs 5,38,872 with 6% interest, taking his disability as 25%. On the insurer's appeal, the High Court in November 2018 cut the disability to 20% and the award to Rs 4,74,072. In August 2024, about eleven and a half years after the accident, the Supreme Court restored the tribunal's award in full.
what_mattered: The doctor who certified 50% permanent disability was examined as a witness, and the tribunal had already taken only half of that (25%) for loss of earning capacity.
The High Court lowered the disability to 20% without a plausible reason; the Supreme Court said a cut in compensation needs some basis in the evidence and restored the tribunal's figure.
